name: high total word count
rationale: Every claude-opus-5 document exceeds 5800 words (range 5875–8945, mean ~6900), while every claude-sonnet-5 document falls below 5700 (range 4355–5611, mean ~5040), a consistent ~37% length premium across all eight document formats.

rule.formula_sketch: Total number of words in the complete document.

name: h3 heading depth prevalence
rationale: claude-opus-5 uses H3 sub-sections across at least five of eight document formats (business-report, case-study, executive-summary, grant-proposal, meeting-minutes), creating consistently deeper heading trees, whereas claude-sonnet-5 rarely nests below H2.

rule.formula_sketch: Number of H3-level headings divided by total number of all headings (H1 + H2 + H3) in the document.

examples: PARA: 62w | The program has the agency's most stable staff.
PARA: 82w | The heart-failure-specific evidence is thin.
PARA: 64w | The consequences are not proportional to the reduction.
PARA: 45w | Enrollment is down 14 percent over six years.
name: short claim opener paragraphs
rationale: claude-opus-5 frequently opens substantial paragraphs with a terse declarative claim (under 12 words) followed by extended elaboration, creating a 'thesis-then-evidence' paragraph shape; claude-sonnet-5 paragraphs of similar length tend to open with longer, more complex sentences that front-load detail.

rule.formula_sketch: Among paragraphs with total word count above 40, count those whose first sentence is 12 words or fewer and forms a complete declarative sentence (not a label or fragment); divide by total paragraphs above 40 words.
